relevance_note: Table S1 of this VEOIBD capsule-endoscopy cohort ties five identifiable patients to a TNFAIP3 genotype ('The frequent mutations were found in TNFAIP3 (n=5)'), so those five are in scope even though no variant description or HA20 diagnosis is printed.
method_note: Read only the paper, schema_ha20_v5.json, extraction_rules_v1.md and extract_v6.md; wrote only the output file and my scratch dir. Scope: the paper is a multicentre retrospective cohort of 37 VEOIBD patients; Table S1 (supplementary file tgh-11-25-22-supplementary.pdf) lists one row per patient per VCE procedure with a Genotype column. Only the five patients whose Genotype cell is TNFAIP3 are in scope (Patients 2, 5, 9, 12, 32); the other 32 patients (BTK, FOXP3, PIK3CD, XIAP, CARD11, SLC37A4, ELANE, BACH2, 'negative') are out of scope and are counted in publications.cohort_size_as_stated = 37. Table S1 is space-aligned: the header spans two lines (Case, Age at VCE, Gender, Genotype, Classification, Duodenum on VCE, Jejunum on VCE, Ileum on VCE, Colonic feature on colonoscopy, Ileal feature on colonoscopy, Gastric feature on gastroscopy, Duodenal bulb feature on gastroscopy, Descending part of the duodenum, Histology, Treatment); I read the aligned rows by hand (no shell available, so no script transcribed the table) and, to avoid reproducing long runs of padding spaces, every span is a short literal that I checked against the markdown: a sentence, or a two-element list giving the row's case label ('Patient 2 VCE 1') and the exact cell content ('ulcer,pus,edema'). Only gene, sex, classification, treatment, age and lesion words were taken from their columns; the lesion words are just the cell contents of that patient's own rows (the segment - duodenum, jejunum, ileum, colon, stomach - was not recorded because no schema field holds it). Uncertainties and notes: (1) No variant description is printed for any patient (the Genotype column gives only the gene), so each variants row keeps variant_original_string 'not reported' (v3 rule); zygosity, inheritance, variant type, pathogenicity and ACMG criteria are 'not reported' because Figure 1 ('identified pathogenic variants') and the Results wording ('mutations') are cohort-level statements that do not name a group of one value for these persons and give no per-person value (v5, D-29). (2) Ages: the only per-person age is 'Age at VCE' per procedure, so age_at_last_evaluation_original_text records the age printed for that patient's last VCE (Patient 2 = 10, Patient 5 = 7, Patient 9 = 6, Patient 12 = 9, Patient 32 = 13); Patient 9's second VCE row has no age printed, so the age of the first (6) is used. Age at onset is not stated per person (the Introduction's 'onset before 6 years of age' is the VEOIBD definition, not a patient fact), so it is 'not reported'. (3) ethnicity_or_country is 'not reported' because only the study's country (China) is stated, not any patient's ancestry or country. (4) 'normal' cells in Table S1 describe a whole examined segment; under D-27 they name no specific abnormality to rule out, so no 'excluded' rows were emitted and no checklist item is 'excluded'. 'not performed' and blank cells were treated as not reported. (5) The group sentence 'All patients with TNFAIP3 mutations except one suffered from ileal ulcers' does not name which patient was the exception, so it was not used to exclude anything; per-patient observed features come from each patient's own Table S1 rows. (6) '4 (10.8%) patients had recurrent infections' gives no names, so no individual was marked for recurrent infections. (7) Contradiction/inconsistency inside the paper: monogenic IBD is '18 patients (48.6%)' in Results but '45% of patients had monogenic IBD' in the Discussion, and Table 1 totals 55 procedures while the text states 58 VCE procedures. (8) is_proband is false (the paper never calls any of these patients a proband or index case) and cites_prior_report_of_same_patients is false (the paper nowhere states that any of its patients were published earlier); neither has a quotable span, so both have span null. (9) HPO candidates are left null because I was not certain of any term or ID. (10) Only macroscopic lesion words from Table S1 were emitted as phenotypic features; histology descriptors (e.g. 'Chronic active enteritis', 'Eosinophil-pattern') and minor qualifiers ('redspot', 'lymphoid changes') were not emitted.

study_type.span: This was a retrospective multicenter study in China to examine the features of VCE among VEOIBD patients.

span: Patients were diagnosed according to previously reported criteria on VEOIBD (14,15).
Next-generation sequencing, including whole exome sequencing or capture-based targeted sequencing were performed.
Next-generation sequencing confirmed the known monogenic IBD in 18 patients (48.6%) (Figure 1).
